newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close narrowly higher.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close narrowly higher.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed fractionally higher Tuesday as trading got off to a slow start after Monday's local holiday, but traders expected the market to regain its momentum in the next few sessions.
"Players were pretty apathetic today, but the undertone remains firm -- I expect fresh gains after this sluggish spell," said Miguel Daneri at traders Boston Securities.

The blue-chip MerVal index edged up 0.3 percent to close at session highs of 805.45. It had rallied 3.2 percent in strong volume last week, closing above 800 points Friday for the first time in almost five years.
The MerVal has dropped only four times in the past month but analysts remain optimistic short-term, based on strong economic growth indicators and an active corporate sector.
"Although conditions are oversold sentiment remains bullish," one analyst said. "Stocks will probably soak up profit-taking and keep stretching higher."
Floor volume shrank to 26.8 million pesos from 42.3 million Friday while over-the-counter turnover dwindled to 83.8 million pesos from 125.9 million Friday.
The broad market index closed up 0.4 percent, with winners outgunning losers 39 to 19 and 29 stocks closing flat.
The top main-tier gainer was pulp and paper maker Celulosa, which jumped 4.2 percent, continuing its rollercoaster ride on slim speculative purchases, dealers said.
Carmaker Sevel rose 3.7 percent on strong local bidding and cement firm Juan Minetti tacked on 2.4 percent.
MerVal losers were led by carmaker Ciadea, steelmaker Siderar and construction stock Polledo, which shed 2.4 percent, 2.0 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
